From d227786ab1119669df4dc333a61510c52047cce4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: HyungJung Joo <jhj140711@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 14:45:56 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] fs/mbcache: cancel shrink work before destroying the cache

mb_cache_destroy() calls shrinker_free() and then frees all cache
entries and the cache itself, but it does not cancel the pending
c_shrink_work work item first.

If mb_cache_entry_create() schedules c_shrink_work via schedule_work()
and the work item is still pending or running when mb_cache_destroy()
runs, mb_cache_shrink_worker() will access the cache after its memory
has been freed, causing a use-after-free.

This is only reachable by a privileged user (root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN)
who can trigger the last put of a mounted ext2/ext4/ocfs2 filesystem.

Cancel the work item with cancel_work_sync() before calling
shrinker_free(), ensuring the worker has finished and will not be
rescheduled before the cache is torn down.

Fixes: c2f3140fe2ec ("mbcache2: limit cache size")
Signed-off-by: Hyungjung Joo <jhj140711@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260317054556.1821600-1-jhj140711@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Christian Brauner <brauner@kernel.org>

diff --git a/fs/mbcache.c b/fs/mbcache.c
index e60a840999aa..90b0564c62d0 100644
--- a/fs/mbcache.c
+++ b/fs/mbcache.c
@@ -408,6 +408,7 @@ void mb_cache_destroy(struct mb_cache *cache)
 {
 	struct mb_cache_entry *entry, *next;
 
+	cancel_work_sync(&cache->c_shrink_work);
 	shrinker_free(cache->c_shrink);

2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications per File

- **fs/mbcache.c**:
  Added a call to `cancel_work_sync(&cache->c_shrink_work)` before the existing `shrinker_free(cache->c_shrink)` in the `mb_cache_destroy()` function.

### Relationship Between Changes

The single change addresses a use-after-free race condition. Previously, `mb_cache_destroy()` would free the cache’s shrinker and then destroy the cache itself without first ensuring that any previously scheduled `c_shrink_work` work item had finished. If `mb_cache_entry_create()` had scheduled this work via `schedule_work()`, the work handler (`mb_cache_shrink_worker()`) could still be running or pending after `shrinker_free()` and the subsequent cache memory deallocation. The added `cancel_work_sync()` guarantees that the work item is either completed or prevented from starting, eliminating the window where the worker could access freed memory. This synchronization is essential for correct cache teardown and prevents the use-after-free vulnerability.

 void mb_cache_destroy(struct mb_cache *cache)
 {
 	struct mb_cache_entry *entry, *next;
 
+	cancel_work_sync(&cache->c_shrink_work);
 	shrinker_free(cache->c_shrink);
 
 	/*
 	 * We don't bother with any locking. Cache must not be used at this
 	 * point.
 	 */
 	list_for_each_entry_safe(entry, next, &cache->c_list, e_list) {
 		list_del(&entry->e_list);
 		WARN_ON(atomic_read(&entry->e_refcnt) != 1);
 		mb_cache_entry_put(cache, entry);
 	}
 	kfree(cache->c_hash);
 	kfree(cache);
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(mb_cache_destroy);
